title: 33 Men, 69 Days Underground: The Full Case of the Chilean Mine Rescue
description:
Case 021, the full case file. On 5 August 2010 the San José copper and gold mine near Copiapó, in Chile's Atacama desert, collapsed and trapped 33 men about 700 metres underground. The road out was sealed, and the ladder in the ventilation shaft had never been finished. In an emergency shelter stocked for about two days they voted on everything and rationed the food: two spoonfuls of tuna, a sip of milk and a bite of cracker each, every other day. Above them, families camped at the gate (Camp Hope) while probe after probe missed. On day 17 a drill came back up with a note tied to it, in red ink: in English, "We are fine in the shelter, the 33 of us." The first estimate for getting them out was four months. Supplies went down the narrow borehole in tubes the rescuers called doves while three drills (Plans A, B and C) cut towards them; Plan B broke through on 9 October. On 13 October 2010 a steel capsule 54 centimetres across lifted them out one at a time in about 22 hours, 69 days after the collapse. Rook didn't believe it either.

Chapters follow the story in order: the note, the collapse, the shelter, the camp, day 17, the lifeline, the three drills, the capsule, the rescue.

Animated reconstruction of a true story. The drill sites, the access road, the ventilation shaft, the gallery, the shelter and the capsule are generic low-poly sets, not models of the real site or equipment; the capsule is drawn as an open cage so the man inside can be seen (the real one was closed), and its white, blue and red bands follow press descriptions of its paint. The miners, rescuers and families are simple figures and nobody's likeness is attempted; no flag, emblem, company name or logo appears. The note card shows an English translation in a drawn hand, not a copy of the real note. The cross-sections and scale drawings are diagrams, not surveys. Staging that is reconstruction, not record: the pickup on the access road, the men running from the dust, how the vote was taken, the queue with cups, the men listening to a drill pass, the hammer on the drill bit, the candles at the camp, how the supply tubes were handled, the shovels and the barrow, the capsule on trestles, who embraces whom, the sack the rocks come out of, the empty gallery, the look of the lid on the shaft, and everything Rook does. Narration is a synthetic voice (Kokoro).

source_notes: IMPORTANT LIMIT OF THIS RUN (17 Nov 2026): the session's network policy refused every page fetch (e-mj.com, wral.com, npr.org, deseret.com, britannica.com and others: host not resolvable), so no page could be opened and read. Only web search worked. The facts the Short already narrates were read on thirteen pages by the Short's run on 16 Nov 2026 and stand on its notes (episodes/r021-sanjose/episode.json). Every fact ADDED here was checked only against what the search tool reported from at least two outlets; it was not read on the page. For that reason this episode is 'ready' (private), not 'approved': the owner or a later run with page access should read the pages before it goes public. Added facts and the outlets the search results gave for them. Mine in operation since 1889 ('more than a century'): Wikipedia, Britannica Kids. Dust blinding the men for hours: Britannica and Wikipedia say up to six hours; the film says 'for hours'. Ventilation shaft, ladder: Britannica ('the ladders required by safety codes were missing'), The World and Interesting Engineering (the owners never finished the ladder; the men got about a third of the way); the film says the ladder 'was never finished' and shows it stopping part-way. Voting: Luis Urzúa, 'Everything was voted on ... 16 plus one was a majority', and Mario Sepúlveda's 'one-man, one-vote' (Wikipedia and pages quoting them); who set the ration is told differently (Urzúa on some pages, Sepúlveda on others), so the film says only that they voted. A sip of milk and a bite of cracker with the tuna: NBC/AP and the Irish Times, from the Short's notes. Heat and damp: figures differ (29 to 35 °C, humidity up to 98% on one page), so the film gives no figure. Water drained from radiators and lamps run from truck batteries: AP via CBS News and Deseret; Maclean's and Wikipedia for the batteries. Camp Hope at the mine gate: The World, PBS NewsHour. Seven misses and the eighth hole near the shelter: the Short's notes. First estimate of up to four months: AP via Fox and HeraldNet. Supply tubes called palomas (doves), first loads glucose gel, rehydration tablets and medicine, then food, letters and a video camera: AP via Washington Times, Scotsman, Fox. Plans A, B and C and the Plan B breakthrough at 8:05 a.m. on 9 October: AP via Washington Times, CNN fast facts, Interesting Engineering, Britannica. Miners clearing the drill cuttings in shifts: Interesting Engineering and trade press; the half-tonne-an-hour figure is on Wikipedia only and is not used. Shaft length 622 to 625 m ('more than six hundred metres') and width 66 to 71 cm; 'about as wide as a bicycle wheel' is this film's comparison, not a quotation. Capsule built by the Chilean navy, 54 cm (21 in) wide: phys.org/AFP, Smithsonian, ABS. Manuel González first rescuer down and last up: Good Morning America, a BBC-derived report, Al Jazeera. First miner (Florencio Ávalos, not named in the film) out at about 12:10 a.m. on 13 October: NPR 12:11, others 'shortly after midnight'; the film says he starts up 'around midnight' and steps out 'just after midnight'. Dark glasses: AP, CNN. The second man up (Mario Sepúlveda, not named) brought rocks as souvenirs: Democracy Now; the LA Times is reported as describing a rock signed by his comrades; the film says 'rocks from the mine, as souvenirs', and the sack is staging. About 22 hours: Al Jazeera 'just 22 hours', Deseret/AP '22½-hour'. Last miner Luis Urzúa: the Short's notes. A lid on the shaft: one page says the president placed a cover on it, NBC mentions 'the lid of the emergency shaft'; its look here is invented. Prosecutors closed the investigation on 1 August 2013 without charges: Irish Times, RTÉ. Left out because one source, or sources differ: the time of day of the collapse, the 50 m² shelter and 2 km of tunnel, weight lost, who wrote the note, what Urzúa said to the president, the number of rescuers who went down, the length of one ride, the television audience, the 2023 compensation ruling, earlier accidents at the mine, the men's names other than Urzúa and González. Not claimed in narration but shown as staging: the men hearing a drill pass (Wikipedia: 'for days the miners had heard drills approaching') and hammering on the bit (Wikipedia: 'tapped on the drill'; one page in the Short's notes).

sound_plan.first_frame: One 'hit' at 0.05 s as a clank on the drill pipe, then a clunk and the scratch of the band; the hook mood is sparse.
sound_plan.music: The engine's score follows the segment moods: hook, tense (doubt), wonder (note), calm (the shift), tense (collapse, ladder, shelter), calm (food, life below), sad (camp, the misses), action (day 17), triumph (alive), tense (re-hook), calm (doves), action (the drills, the breakthrough), calm (capsule), tense (rescuer down), wonder (the ride), triumph (out, the count), calm, end.
sound_plan.hush: The music is pulled out under shot 57 (his face in the cage, the light growing).
sound_plan.tragic_beats: Nobody dies in this story. The camp and the misses (66 to 83 s) are 'sad' segments: no pulse, a low tone and a heartbeat; Rook is still, with his brim down.
sound_plan.effects: Clunks for steel on steel (drill, capsule, ladder), scratches for grit and paper, shouts and gasps only where mouths open, ticks for counted things, engine for the rigs and the pickup, wind on the last site shot. No effect without a visible cause.
sound_plan.voice: Narration is ducked over the bed by the engine; the rehearsal measured it, it was not listened to.

quality_gate.access: What was inspected: a low-res contact sheet of every 3D shot (round 1), the composited cards, captions and labels (round 1), the thumbnail at full size (three versions), and full-length rehearsals (three complete renders and three partial re-renders, six gate runs; 384x216, 4 samples, 6 fps 3D frames composited at 12 fps with captions, labels, overlays, inserts and sound), each reviewed as a 2-frames-per-second sheet of the whole video (384 frames). Not done: no playback at speed; the audio was measured, not listened to; no frame was rendered at 1280x720 locally. The cloud render is the first full-resolution, 60 fps pass.
quality_gate.method: Round 1 (contact sheet, 59 3D stills; composited cards). Found and fixed: Rook with his back to the camera or hiding the action in the muck, workshop, dove and first-rescuer shots; the cave-in too wide and dim; a dust cloud in front of the lens; the battery shot blown out white; the three rigs too far away; the rescuer hiding Rook in the second note shot; the lid a speck; the empty gallery too dark to see the capsule; the Short's cut-away shaft small in a wide frame; a label over the road in the cross-section; the thumbnail's subject under its own words. Round 2 (first full rehearsal): the gate FAILED locally on four static stretches (the case-file card, the count card, the lid shot, the board) and a slow first second. Fixed in the film, not in the gate: the cards push in and sway with moving light and dust, the opening swings round the note and shakes, Rook walks up to the lid, every 3D shot swings round its subject. Also fixed: a miner's back filling the frame in the pickup shot, an arch post across the lens on day 17, the hook words over the miners' helmets. Round 3 (second rehearsal, gate PASS): the thumbnail's words ran off the left edge and the face was behind the pipe; the walking miners walked into the lens in the second pickup shot; Rook hidden behind the capsule on the trestles; a date label clipped on the count card. Round 4 (third rehearsal, gate PASS): the camera passed through the tunnel wall at the end of the second pickup shot and through the locker at the start of the empty-gallery shot; both fixed, more movement given to the lid shot and the second derrick shot (the two thinnest margins), and those four shots rendered and gated again. Round 5: that gate run FAILED on the second pickup shot (22 to 26 s), which the fix had left too still; it was restaged as a drive-past (the camera stands in the road, the miners and the truck come up and pass), its first second was then found to start behind a wall rock, the camera was moved clear, and the last rehearsal was composited and gated from the final files.
quality_gate.gate_result: Last rehearsal, composited from the final files: local gate PASS. 71 shots, mean 2.70 s, longest 4.75 s, first shot 1.85 s; Rook acting in 37 of 71 shots (52%); -14.5 LUFS, peak -1.2 dBFS, voice 14.9 dB over the bed; closest match to any earlier episode 0.72 (shot 7, the note card, against r005-vulovic-long; the limit is 0.93); mean frame change 2.46; first second 2.65 (floor 2.0); lowest 3.5 s stretches without a detected cut: 1.02 at 165.8 s (the count card), 1.10 at 176.2 s (the empty gallery), 1.13 at 72.7 s (the derrick at night), 1.29 at 108.7 s and 180.7 s (floor 0.8). Duration 191.8 s (3 min 12 s). 606 words in 25 segments. The rehearsal's fingerprint file was deleted, not committed; the cloud render runs the real gate at 1280x720 and 60 fps.
quality_gate.checked: Every kind in the storyboard exists in world3d.SHOTS3D or scenes.SHOTS (the compositor refuses to run otherwise); HOST lists every kind in which Rook is placed (37 of 71 shots, 52%); no kind is used more than twice and none twice in a row. Re-hook at 49%. One hush shot (57). On-screen dates, names and figures against the sources: 22 AUGUST 2010, SAN JOSÉ MINE, CHILE, 5 AUGUST 2010, ATACAMA DESERT, COPPER AND GOLD, 33 MEN, 700 M, 2 SPOONFULS, EVERY OTHER DAY, CAMP HOPE, 7 MISSED, DAY 17, 33 ALIVE, FIRST ESTIMATE: 4 MONTHS, THE DOVES, GLUCOSE, MEDICINE, FOOD, PLAN A/B/C, 9 OCTOBER 2010, 620 M +, 54 CM ACROSS, MANUEL GONZÁLEZ, RESCUER, 13 OCTOBER 2010, AROUND MIDNIGHT, JUST AFTER MIDNIGHT, 33 OF 33, 69 DAYS, LUIS URZÚA, SHIFT FOREMAN, and the four dates on the 69-day line (9 October is day 65). The cross-sections are marked DIAGRAM, NOT TO SCALE. Nobody dies in this story and nothing graphic is shown. No flag, emblem, logo, lettering or likeness appears on any set or person.
quality_gate.not_met: Fact checking: no web page could be opened in this session (network policy), so the added facts rest on search results from two or more outlets and were not read on the page; this is why the status is 'ready'. No playback and no listening. No local frame at 1280x720. The 13-category score is from stills and rehearsal sheets. The gate's margin on movement is thin in the rehearsal on a few held shots (see gate_result), and rehearsal frames are noisier than the cloud render, so the real gate could still fail there; if it does, the fix is more movement in those shots, not a change to the gate. A dark frame at the start of the ventilation-shaft shot in the 2 fps sheets is the engine's whip transition, not a missing picture (the 3D frame was looked at).

review.weakest: The ventilation shaft and the cut-away shaft have black on both sides of a wide frame. The dust in the cave-in is low-poly lumps and reads as boulders as much as dust. The vote is filmed from far enough that the raised hands are small. The supply tube is thin and easy to miss on the surface. Several gallery shots share one look. Figures' hands cannot hold things convincingly (shovels, hammer, letter). respect_accuracy is 3 only because of how the added facts were checked. Narration and sound were measured, not heard.
